title: Cloudflare Introduces Cache Response Rules for Post-Origin Cache Control
gist: Cloudflare added Cache Response Rules, a new rules-engine phase that runs after the origin responds but before content is written to cache, letting customers strip Set-Cookie/ETag/Last-Modified headers and rewrite Cache-Control without touching the origin application. It is available on all Cloudflare plans, positioning edge-side cache repair as a free lever for raising hit ratios and cutting origin bandwidth.

insights.claim: Cloudflare has introduced Cache Response Rules, a rules engine that executes after an origin server responds but before content is written to Cloudflare's cache, creating a response-evaluation phase that did not previously exist in its CDN pipeline.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A structural extension of Cloudflare's rules engine widens the surface where it can capture configuration lock-in versus rival CDNs.
insights.quote: a rules engine that operates after an origin server responds but before content is written to Cloudflare's cache
insights.locator: Cloudflare recently introduced Cache Response Rules

insights.claim: Cloudflare's cache decisions are now explicitly two-phase: request-time Cache Rules decide whether and how to look up content before contacting the origin, while Cache Response Rules get the final say on caching once the origin's response is seen.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A two-phase mental model for edge caching is the frame to judge competing CDN feature sets against.
insights.quote: Cache Rules decide whether, what, and how we cache on the request. Cache Response Rules get the final word on the how and whether, once the origin's response is seen by Cloudflare in a phase that didn't exist before.
insights.locator: The team clarifies why they are complementary

insights.claim: Cache Response Rules ship with exactly three actions at launch: removing headers that interfere with caching, managing cache tags, and modifying Cache-Control directives.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A narrow three-action v1 signals an early-stage feature with obvious room for paid expansion later.
insights.locator: Cache Response Rules currently support three actions

themes.theme: Stray headers as a cost leak

insights.claim: A single accidental Set-Cookie header on a static asset makes it uncacheable at every Cloudflare data center, and Cloudflare frames this multiplied across visitors and sites as a cache-hit-ratio problem that leaks origin bandwidth and drives infrastructure costs higher.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Frames misconfigured headers, not capacity, as a leading driver of origin egress spend — a cost line that edge fixes can compress without new hardware.
insights.quote: you have a cache hit ratio that is leaking origin bandwidth, ruining performance, and driving infrastructure costs higher.
insights.locator: The asset that should have been cached at every Cloudflare data center

insights.claim: Cloudflare's stated motivation is that cache-breaking headers such as Set-Cookie and wrong Cache-Control values are sometimes hard or impossible to strip at the origin itself, making the edge the only practical fix point.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Legacy origin applications that cannot be changed are the durable demand pool for edge-side configuration products.
insights.quote: headers that are sometimes hard or impossible to strip or change on the origin itself, then Cache Response Rules is that fix, applied at exactly the right moment.

insights.claim: Cloudflare positions Cache Response Rules as simplifying CDN migrations, since customers can normalise cache headers at the edge rather than re-engineering origin applications to match a new provider's expectations.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Lowering switching cost onto Cloudflare is a share-capture lever aimed at incumbent CDN estates like Akamai and Fastly customers.

insights.claim: Cache Response Rules are available across all Cloudflare plans rather than gated to enterprise tiers.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Free-tier distribution of an origin-cost-saving feature buys adoption breadth over near-term ARPU — watch whether advanced actions later move behind a paywall.
insights.quote: Cache Response Rules are available across all Cloudflare plans.
insights.locator: Cache Response Rules are available across all Cloudflare plans

insights.claim: Practitioner commentary reported around the launch argues that improving cache performance is mainly a matter of optimizing response behavior rather than adding more infrastructure, cutting origin load without code changes.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: If configuration beats capacity for a meaningful share of workloads, marginal compute and bandwidth demand from web serving is softer than headline traffic growth implies.
insights.quote: Improving cache performance often comes down to optimizing response behavior rather than adding more infrastructure.

insights.claim: Some practitioners pushed back on the launch, warning that forcing caching at the edge is risky if engineers incorrectly classify dynamic content as cacheable.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Correctness risk from overriding origin intent is the main adoption brake and a likely source of future incident headlines.
insights.quote: While some practitioners expressed skepticism about forcing caching if engineers incorrectly classify dynamic content as cacheable

insights.claim: The appeal cited by adopters is the ability to fix origin mistakes at the edge without waiting on application changes, decoupling infrastructure optimisation from the application release cycle.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: FinOps buyers, not just platform engineers, are becoming a purchasing constituency for edge features — relevant to how CDN vendors sell.
insights.quote: Fixing origin mistakes at the edge, without waiting on app changes, is a big win.
